evals.title: polynesian-spread
evals.tagline: Model how Polynesians crossed the Pacific — then simulate the voyaging it took.
evals.description: Build a computer model of how the Polynesians spread from the Austronesian homeland out to Hawaiʻi, Rapa Nui, and Aotearoa, grounded in the real record: radiocarbon and settlement dates, genetic dating, linguistic phylogeny, and Pacific oceanography (winds, currents, ENSO reversals, swell, inter-island distances). Then make the model runnable — let an evaluator change voyaging assumptions (boat speed and range, upwind ability, provisioning, navigation, return voyages) and watch which regimes reproduce the archaeologically-attested spread within the time frames the evidence allows, and which fail. Ship one committed static HTML page that is both the world model and the simulation, surfaces the contested questions (the West Polynesia long pause, the tempo of the East Polynesian expansion, upwind vs. downwind colonization), and stays inspectable through maps, timelines, and traces. The headline question: what were the boats and the voyaging strategy capable of?

solutions.summary: A single-file, offline 'Wayfinders' Atlas' that is both a sourced world model of the Austronesian/Polynesian spread and a runnable, falsifiable voyaging simulation. The world model is 21 island nodes from the real record (out-of-Taiwan origin; the Lapita pulse through the Bismarcks, Solomons, Vanuatu, New Caledonia and Fiji into Remote Oceania; West Polynesia at Tonga/Samoa ~2850 BP; the ~1,800-year West Polynesian 'long pause'; the explosive East Polynesian pulse ~AD 1000-1300; and the three corners Hawaiʻi, Rapa Nui and Aotearoa), each carrying a settlement-evidence window shown as a range with a cited note (Wilmshurst et al. 2011, Burley et al. 2012, Hunt & Lipo 2006, Skoglund et al. 2016, etc.). Over that it lays a legible physics layer — analytic trade winds, equatorial counter-flow, ENSO westerly windows and surface currents, plus a canoe polar (speed, provisioning range, windward ability, navigation/landfall skill) — and a Dijkstra shortest-arrival-time solver that computes when, if ever, the spread reaches each island. The page renders an animated map (winds/currents/voyage tracks/failed crossings), a settlement timeline against the evidence windows with the long-pause band drawn in, a per-hop run trace showing the limiting physics, a click-any-island route inspector, a verdict, and World-model / Debates / Sources tabs. Four presets make it falsifiable: weatherly two-way wayfinding reproduces the record; drift-only (Sharp 1956) fails to enter East Polynesia (cf. Levison, Ward & Webb 1973); marginal range reaches the EP core but strands the far corners; heavy-ENSO windows are an alternative success path.

outcome.verdict: Commits a single self-contained index.html (vanilla JS + HTML5 canvas, no dependencies, no network) that renders the full world model and simulation from a fresh clone, and mirrors it under public/artifacts for one-click review. Reads the spread with sourced, uncertainty-ranged dates (radiocarbon/tephra/genetics/linguistics) and surfaces the contested questions in a Debates tab. The simulation is genuinely falsifiable: sliders and presets produce regimes that fail (pure drift never enters East Polynesia; marginal range strands Hawaiʻi and Rapa Nui) and regimes that succeed (weatherly two-way voyaging; frequent ENSO windows), and every result is traceable to the winds, currents, distances and decision rules via the map overlays, run trace, and per-island route inspector.

solutions.notes: Open `polynesian-spread/cursor-fable-5-thinking-high/index.html` directly in a desktop browser, or use the mirrored artifact at `./artifacts/polynesian-spread/cursor-fable-5-thinking-high.html`. Change the voyaging sliders (windward ability, provisioning range, ENSO windows, two-way voyaging) or click a preset, then Run spread; click any island to inspect why each route is feasible or blocked.

evals.title: surf-lodge-scout
evals.tagline: Scout real Hawaiian listings for a surf lodge — with satellite receipts.
evals.description: Act as a site scout for an investor with a $4M acquisition budget who wants a boutique Hawaiian surf lodge. Find real, currently-listed properties, scout them from satellite/aerial imagery, ground the surf story in real swell and buoy data, surface Hawaii's deal-breakers (lava zones, tsunami and flood zones, zoning, leasehold vs fee simple), and deliver one committed static HTML page that makes a persuasive, verifiable case for where to put the money. How the narrative is assembled is up to the agent — persuasiveness grounded in checkable evidence (live listing links, coordinates that hold up in Google Maps) is the judging axis.

solutions.summary: An investor pitch, 'The Last Legal Lodge', whose thesis is regulatory rather than romantic: since 2022 Oahu, Kauai, and Maui have outlawed or are phasing out nightly lodging outside resort zones, so the scout screens for legality first and lands on Kailua-Kona's Alii Drive corridor (Big Island), where resort V-1.25 zoning and grandfathered STVR registrations still permit a lodge near year-round surf. Verdict: 78-111-A Holua Rd, Keauhou ($4.45M ask after two cuts; offer $3.9M, walk at $4.2M) - a fee-simple 5BR + studio compound sleeping 14, a 150 m walk above He'eia Bay - with a backup position on a $1.895M oceanfront V-zoned home under contract. Every parcel was verified against official State of Hawaii GIS layers (zoning, SMA, lava, tsunami, FEMA flood), which surfaced that the pick's 'resort zone' marketing is wrong (it is RS-10 with a registration that lapses 90 days after sale - so the offer is written contingent on re-registration), and rejects the beautiful traps (Sunset Beach erosion strip, Hanalei flood/VDA ban, a $4.2M Kona oceanfront two parcels outside the legal zone) with five locally-stored annotated satellite exhibits and a paste-into-Google-Maps coordinates appendix.

outcome.verdict: Commits a self-contained index.html (satellite exhibits load from a local img/ folder, so it renders fully offline) plus a base64-embedded single-file mirror under public/artifacts for one-click review. Listings are real and live as of the stated scouting date (June 10, 2026) with MLS numbers and links; parcel, zoning, and hazard claims are reproducible from committed GIS query scripts and raw responses; coordinates in the appendix land on the claimed sites.

solutions.notes: Open `surf-lodge-scout/cursor-fable-5-thinking-high/index.html` directly in a desktop browser, or use the mirrored artifact at `./artifacts/surf-lodge-scout/cursor-fable-5-thinking-high.html`. Judge listing prices/statuses against the stated scouting date of June 10, 2026.

evals.title: gaps-get-filled
evals.tagline: Backtest S&P 500 gap-fills, grid-search params, and argue the folklore.
evals.description: Build a backtesting sandbox and CLI, actually execute backtests on U.S. equities (S&P 500 / 10-year minimum), run a documented parameter grid search, and specify the experiments (fixed vs. varied dimensions, metrics). Ship a self-contained HTML presentation with comparative visualizations of how configurations perform, not only a single-run narrative — plus a clear position on what the result means.

solutions.summary: Python + pandas backtesting sandbox with strict-gap detection, an event-driven single-symbol backtester, and a static HTML presentation generator. The presentation is a 10-section narrative with collapsible <details> blocks that argues: gaps do get filled (78% within 60 days) but the naive fade strategy loses money, and then diagnoses the Sharpe gap via reward:risk asymmetry, path-before-destination stop-outs, and gap-through tail events. Streamlit dashboard also included for ad-hoc exploration.

outcome.verdict: Ships a precomputed 7-symbol / 10-year demo run and sample dashboard.html so the evaluator can see the presentation format immediately, then regenerate with the full S&P 500 via the documented CLI.

solutions.notes: Live demo (deployed): [./artifacts/gaps-get-filled/claude-code-opus-4-7-high.html](./artifacts/gaps-get-filled/claude-code-opus-4-7-high.html). In-repo copy at `results/runs/test_7sym/dashboard.html`. Regenerate any run's HTML with `python scripts/build_dashboard.py --run <name>`.

solutions.summary: Python + uv backtesting sandbox with a strict-gap hypothesis tester, reusable strategy interface, CLI commands for download/backtest/present/grid-search, and a self-contained HTML presentation that explicitly argues: the folklore is empirically supported over longer horizons, but a naive fade still struggles on Sharpe because the path to the fill is too noisy.

outcome.verdict: Ships a committed HTML presentation and mirrors it into the docs artifact path for one-click evaluation. The presentation distinguishes the empirical fill-rate claim from the weaker claim that a naive gap-fade is actually tradeable.

solutions.notes: Open the in-repo presentation at `gaps-get-filled/cursor-gpt-5-4/gpt-5-4-backtesting/results/sp500-10y/presentation/report.html` or the mirrored artifact at `./artifacts/gaps-get-filled/cursor-gpt-5-4.html`.

solutions.summary: Python + uv backtesting sandbox with strict range-gap detection, a reusable strategy interface, local per-symbol caching, and a narrative HTML report generator. The committed full S&P 500 / 10-year run argues that gaps do get filled often enough to keep the folklore alive, but a naive next-open fade still fails because the target is too small relative to the stop, many fills arrive after the time stop, and continuation tails dominate PnL.

outcome.verdict: Ships a committed full-run HTML artifact built from 503 live S&P 500 constituents across a 10-year window, plus mirrored Pages output for one-click review. The narrative makes a clear case: 73.1% of strict gaps fill within 60 trading days and 90.0% eventually fill, yet the naive fade still posts a negative Sharpe.

solutions.summary: Single-file Three.js life sim. Seeded Perlin-noise island with meadow / forest / rock / sand / snow biomes, a custom-shader sky that crossfades dawn → noon → dusk → night with stars, and a wavy water shader that tints by night. Three roles (Leafers, Stalkers, Tide Sprites) act via a sensing-based FSM (wander / forage / flee / pursue / mate / rest) over a spatial hash. Each organism carries an 8-gene genome (size, speed, sense, metabolism, armor, aggression, fertility, nocturnal) that drives both behavior weights and visible body (scaled limbs, head, ears, fins, tail, spines, tint). Reproduction is uniform-crossover + gaussian mutation; no fitness function is imposed. Night gives Stalkers up to +60% sense range and +20% speed, so the nocturnal gene becomes a real selection knob. HUD includes population / births-vs-deaths / per-species trait-drift / generation-depth charts, click-to-inspect, event log, and an in-app 'How it works' explainer. Speed slider + presets + keyboard shortcuts.

outcome.verdict: Commits a browser-playable HTML simulation directly in the solution folder and mirrors it under docs/artifacts for one-click results site evaluation.
